 Racing against time on urgent projects
 (GLO) - Among the 64 emergency projects to mitigate the consequences of Typhoon No. 13 and the floods in November 2025, many dikes and embankments have been completed, but some projects remain unfinished as the rainy season approaches.
 Báo Gia Lai • 26/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Local authorities, investors, and contractors are accelerating progress, resolving obstacles, and simultaneously controlling quality, ensuring project safety, and maintaining flood drainage capacity.
 In Cam Van residential area (An Nhon Dong ward), Mr. Le Van Minh (59 years old) still remembers the worry he felt every time the rainy season came, when the riverbanks eroded, threatening his house.
 Previously, his house wall was only about 3 meters from the riverbank, posing a risk of landslides that could affect the foundation. To expedite the project, his family voluntarily donated over 50 square meters of land.
 After more than two months of construction, the embankment is gradually taking shape. "Now, our house has a spacious frontage overlooking the river," Mr. Minh said happily.
 The Cam Van River embankment is included in the list of urgent construction projects according to Decision No. 167/QD-UBND dated January 14, 2026, of the Chairman of the Provincial People's Committee.
 The project is part of a 161 billion VND budget from the provincial reserve fund aimed at repairing damage to 64 dikes, river embankments, sea embankments, lakes, dams, and canals caused by Typhoon No. 13 and subsequent floods.
 According to the plan, canal and dam projects must ensure irrigation for the Winter-Spring crop before January 31, 2026; the remaining projects will be completed in 2026.
 Accelerate construction and resolve land clearance issues.
 To date, many projects have been basically completed or have achieved a fairly high volume of construction. In An Nhon Dong ward, 5 out of 6 projects have been put into use; the Cam Van river embankment has reached about 90% completion. 
 The Xuan Thanh embankment (Phu My Dong commune) has reached nearly 87% of its contract value; the Ca Cong and Ca Cong Nam embankments (Hoai Nhon Dong ward) have reached approximately 70%. Meanwhile, the An Lao river embankment section from My Thanh bridge to Nang An village (Van Duc commune) has reached about 75% of its volume.
 In An Nhon Dong ward, six projects with a total capital of nearly 32 billion VND (4.2 billion VND supported by the provincial budget, the rest contributed by the local government). Mr. Cao Tan Si - a technical officer of the Ward's Public Service and Land Development Management Board - said that as of October 22nd, five projects had been completed and put into use. 
 The Cam Van river embankment, from Cam Tien 2 bridge to the border with Chin Chau embankment (An Nhon Dong ward), is nearing completion. Photo: Provided. You may also like The remaining project is the Cam Van river embankment, the section from Cam Tien 2 bridge to the Chin Chau embankment, 255 meters long, with an investment of over 5.3 billion VND. Land clearance issues are affecting the progress. The contractor is currently compacting the foundation to construct the crest beams and embankment surface, striving to complete it in October 2026.
 Similarly, the Xuan Thanh embankment (Phu My Dong commune) still has about 20 meters left unconstructed due to land clearance issues related to a petition from a local resident.
 Mr. Phan Quang Nghia, Director of the Phu My Dong Commune Management Board, said that the local authorities had responded to the request, but the households had not yet complied. The government is considering a plan to protect the construction site to resolve the issue definitively, striving to complete the project in October 2026.
 In Van Duc commune, the An Lao river embankment, initially over 800 meters long, was later extended by approximately 150 meters, bringing the total length to nearly 1 kilometer. According to the Chairman of the Commune People's Committee, Nguyen Hoai Nguyen, the adjustment in scale and prolonged rain caused the roadbed to become soft, hindering the construction of some outdoor items.
 Currently, the investor and contractor are focusing on completing the embankment foundation, installing beams and frames, and then pouring concrete for the embankment surface. Taking advantage of favorable weather, the construction crew is laying and compacting the road section on the embankment, minimizing the risk of damage when rain and floods occur. The project is expected to be substantially completed by the end of January 2027.
 Under pressure to meet deadlines, the Department of Agriculture and Environment requested localities and investors to mobilize manpower, machinery, and materials, and organize construction in multiple shifts; prioritizing the completion of underwater items, embankment foundations, embankment slopes, dam bodies, and vulnerable locations before river and stream water levels rise. 
 Mr. Ngo Vinh Khanh, Head of the Irrigation Sub-Department (Department of Agriculture and Environment), emphasized that strengthening construction efforts must go hand in hand with controlling water flow, avoiding narrowing of riverbeds and streams, which would affect flood drainage capacity, especially during the rainy season. Temporary structures must be strictly managed, promptly removed, and prevented from encroaching on riverbeds, streams, and dike protection corridors.
 We will not compromise quality for speed.
 At the Hai Minh seawall construction site, residential area 1 (Quy Nhon ward), in the last days of October 2026, 15 workers along with machinery were urgently constructing the seawall slope paving and drainage system.
 According to Mr. Phan Khac Duy, Director of the Ward Management Board, the embankment, which is over 262 meters long, started construction on July 3rd and is expected to be completed in February 2027. 
 The Hai Minh seawall, residential area 1 (Quy Nhon ward), is expected to be completed in February 2027. Photo: Provided. Expediting construction must go hand in hand with quality and safety. The Department of Agriculture and Environment requires control over the origin and quality of materials; and the removal of cracked or broken components that do not meet design requirements.
 Acceptance testing must comply with technical regulations and standards. For contractors who perform poorly or fall behind schedule, the investor must address the contract violations or transfer the work to a more capable unit.
 You may also like According to Vu Ngoc An, Deputy Director of the Department of Agriculture and Environment, local authorities must regularly inspect the site and promptly resolve any issues related to land, materials, and personnel.
 The Chairpersons of the People's Committees of communes and wards are responsible to the Chairperson of the Provincial People's Committee if projects are delayed, unsafe, or result in capital losses. Localities must report by the 25th of each month on the volume of work completed, difficulties encountered, and completion deadlines; acceptance and payment will be based on actual work volume, avoiding the concentration of funds at the end of the year.
 For completed projects, post- heavy rain inspections should also be maintained to detect and address early signs of embankment slope subsidence, embankment base erosion, and leakage. 
 Ms. Nguyen Thi Ngoc Lan (57 years old, residing in Cam Van residential area, An Nhon Dong ward) hopes that the authorities will continue to clear the waterway downstream of Cam Tien 2 bridge to allow water to drain faster during floods, contributing to the protection of the residential area.
 The rainy and stormy season doesn't wait for construction sites. Therefore, in addition to accelerating construction, localities need to definitively resolve obstacles, control quality, and proactively prepare for adverse weather conditions.
 Each completed project, on schedule and with guaranteed safety, will contribute to protecting riverbanks, coastlines, and residential areas from the unpredictable effects of rain and floods.
